import math

# Data from page 17 of Treasury Bulletin January 1941
# Individual and Corporation income tax collections (in thousands)

# January 1940
jan_individual = 20561
jan_corporation = 25128

# February 1940
feb_individual = 43443
feb_corporation = 27503

# March 1940
mar_individual = 356076
mar_corporation = 298548

# Calculate ratios (individual / corporation)
ratio_jan = jan_individual / jan_corporation
ratio_feb = feb_individual / feb_corporation
ratio_mar = mar_individual / mar_corporation

print("Ratios (Individual/Corporation):")
print(f"January 1940: {ratio_jan:.6f}")
print(f"February 1940: {ratio_feb:.6f}")
print(f"March 1940: {ratio_mar:.6f}")

# Linear regression: months (1,2,3) vs ratios
# x values: 1, 2, 3
# y values: ratio_jan, ratio_feb, ratio_mar

x = [1, 2, 3]
y = [ratio_jan, ratio_feb, ratio_mar]

n = len(x)
sum_x = sum(x)
sum_y = sum(y)
sum_xy = sum([x[i]*y[i] for i in range(n)])
sum_x2 = sum([x[i]**2 for i in range(n)])

# Calculate slope
slope = (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x**2)

# Calculate intercept
intercept = (sum_y - slope * sum_x) / n

print(f"\nLinear Regression Results:")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f}")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f}")
print(f"\nSlope rounded to thousandths: {round(slope, 3)}")

# Also verify the fit
for i in range(n):
    print(f"Month {x[i]}: actual = {y[i]:.6f}, predicted = {slope*x[i] + intercept:.6f}")
